statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 12% (low), Stress 51% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high). Nasdaq-100 futures hold the upper edge of a narrow overnight band on thin Asian liquidity, with VIX, Treasury yields and crude showing no amplifier alignment ahead of a heavily scheduled U.S. Friday.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window is 13:30-16:00 UTC (15:30-18:00 Berlin), covering the U.S. cash open, Chicago PMI and the simultaneous 14:00 UTC Warsh keynote, payroll benchmark revision and final Michigan sentiment, where the mapped forecast state moves to WATCH. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures press the top of a narrow overnight band before Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Thursday at 29,641.56, up 1.43%, finishing at the upper edge of its 29,366.42-29,643.53 range after Nvidia rose 8.74% on results and a revenue outlook well above consensus. Leadership was narrow rather than broad: only 156 of the 503 S&P 500 members advanced and 23 of the 30 Dow components fell, so the advance was carried by a handful of mega-cap technology names. Since the close, NQ futures have held a band of roughly 29,592-29,701 - about 0.37% wide - and were last near 29,699, essentially unchanged and pressing the top of that band on thin Asian-session liquidity. That is a quiet drift rather than persistent directional efficiency: the band is narrow, no failed retracement sequence has formed, and the move has produced no cross-asset confirmation. VIX closed at 14.51, down 4.60%; the 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields ended Aug 27 at 4.20% and 4.67%, each about one basis point higher; WTI is near $83.15 and Brent near $88.24, both slightly softer. Asia is mixed, with the Nikkei 225 up 0.82% and the Kospi down 1.14%, and Marvell fell more than 7% after hours despite beating on the quarter and guiding above consensus, which sets a two-sided semiconductor tone into Friday rather than a one-way one. Tail therefore stays low. Stress is elevated because the U.S. session concentrates several catalysts into a single window: Chicago PMI at 13:45 UTC, then Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote, the BLS preliminary payroll benchmark revision and final Michigan sentiment all at 14:00 UTC, on the last business day of August with month-end rebalancing flows in the tape. A first keynote from a new Chair is structurally multi-stage, so the conditional risk is a delayed second leg through yields into equities rather than the initial reaction. Confidence is high: current futures pricing, the cash close, VIX, Treasury yields, crude, the Asian session and the verified U.S. calendar were all obtained from primary or reputable current sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 clock-hours every published Claude assessment stayed in the EA_ON band, with Tail between 10% and 14% and Stress ranging from the mid-40s during the European morning to the low 50s around the U.S. session and overnight. The dominant mode was predominantly mixed, with two trend-up marks at 17:00 and 20:00 UTC as the Nvidia-led advance extended into the cash close, and one unavailable hour at 09:00 UTC on 27 August where no assessment was published. No hour reached the watch band, and the series shows no episode of persistent no-retracement structure over the period.
outlookSummary: The horizon runs from a quiet late-Asian session through the European morning into a concentrated U.S. afternoon and then the weekend futures halt. Conditional risk builds gradually from 06:00 UTC on European positioning and month-end flows, steps up at the 13:30 UTC cash open and 13:45 UTC Chicago PMI, and peaks across 14:00-16:00 UTC on the Warsh keynote, the payroll benchmark revision and final Michigan sentiment, where the mapped state moves to WATCH before decaying back to EA_ON. Scores normalise through the U.S. afternoon, rise modestly into the 20:00 UTC month-end close, and then fall to a closed-market baseline once CME equity index futures halt at 21:00 UTC for the weekend.
